sources.title: Request: monthly review trigger in Africa/Luanda with a clear missed-run policy

workflows.name: Monthly review

access.note: No grants proposed yet: the reviewing team is not identified (D2). Until it is, only the importer and organization administrators see the cases; the scheduled case is created without a start grant.

schedule.reason: Monthly cadence from the request; day and hour are assumptions (D3); catch-up-one is the proposed missed-run policy (D4).

unresolvedActors.name: Monthly reviewer
unresolvedActors.detail: The team or role that performs the review is not named in the request (D2). The action has no assignee until it is.

actions.name: Conduct the monthly review
evidence: Completed checklist or review report attached as a file (recommendation: the request names no evidence)
Each finding recorded in a comment with a named owner

setupNotes: Schedule trigger: cron `0 8 1 * *`, timezone Africa/Luanda (UTC+01:00, no daylight saving, so 08:00 Luanda is 07:00 UTC all year), missedBehavior `catch-up-one`. Confirm in the destination organization that the schedule shows the next run on the 1st at 08:00 Luanda time.

Missed-run policy: a slot missed while the scheduler was unavailable opens exactly one case on recovery (`catch-up-one`); several missed months still produce one case and the reviewer covers them all, recording the months in `review_period`. Verify in the destination product how far back the catch-up window reaches; the bundled contract fixes the option names, not the window.

Manual trigger «Open an out-of-cycle review» has no allowlist yet because the reviewing team is unknown (D2). Restrict it to that team in Provia once named; until then every holder of create_incident (only the importer and administrators under creator_only) can start it.
Assign `conduct-review` to the reviewing team in Provia before publication (validator item `assignment_missing`). No group id was invented.
`due` of 5 workdays from activation is an illustrative service level (D5); workdays skip Saturday and Sunday only, not Angolan public holidays.

No HTTP call, secret or destination allowlist is part of this design. If the review must read data from an external system, its API contract is required first (see monthly-review-trigger-spec.md, section 7).
Overdue escalation: once the recipient is decided (D6), add a notification action or a Provia overdue rule; none is emitted now because notification recipients need real group ids.

decisions.question: Which process does the monthly review belong to and what exactly is reviewed (scope, source records, checklist)? The request names none.
Which group performs the review? Needed for the action assignee, the manual-trigger allowlist and the access grants.
Run on the 1st of each month at 08:00 Luanda time (proposed), or another day/hour? Numeric cron cannot express «last day of the month» or «first working day».

Confirm the missed-run policy: `catch-up-one` (proposed: one case on recovery, reviewer covers every missed month) or `catch-up-all` (one case per missed month, needed only if audit evidence must exist per month as a separate case). `skip` is not recommended because a missed month would leave no trace.
What is the service level for completing the review? 5 workdays from case creation is illustrative.
Who is informed when a review case is overdue, and through which channel (in-app, email)?
Does the review need to be linked to an entity (for example a supplier, contract or cost centre) or to read data from an external system? If so, the entity type or the API contract is required.
